Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
polvo
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian polve, from Latin pulvis (“dust, powder”). Compare German Pulver (“powder”), French poudre (“powder”), English powder.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpolvo/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Audio 3:(file)
  • Rhymes: -olvo
  • Syllabification: pol‧vo

Noun

[edit]

polvo (accusative singular polvon, plural polvoj, accusative plural polvojn)

  1. dust

Derived terms

[edit]
  • polva
  • polvi
  • polvosuĉi
  • polvoŝtormo

Further reading

[edit]
  • “polvo”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “polvo”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-present

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Esperanto polvo, Italian polvere, Spanish polvo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpolvo/

Noun

[edit]

polvo (plural polvi)

  1. powder, dust

Derived terms

[edit]
  • polvoza (“dusty”)
  • senpolvigar (“to dust”)

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
polvo
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese polbo, from Latin polypus (“octopus”), from Ancient Greek πολύπους (polúpous). Doublet of pólipo.

Cognate with Galician polbo, Spanish pulpo, Italian polpo, French poulpe, pieuvre.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpow.vu/ [ˈpoʊ̯.vu]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpow.vu/ [ˈpoʊ̯.vu]
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpow.vo/ [ˈpoʊ̯.vo]
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈpol.vu/ [ˈpoɫ.vu]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈpol.vu/ [ˈpoɫ.vu]
    • (Northern Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈpol.bu/ [ˈpoɫ.βu]

  • Hyphenation: pol‧vo

Noun

[edit]

polvo m (plural polvos, metaphonic)

  1. octopus

Related terms

[edit]
  • pólipo

Further reading

[edit]
  • “polvo”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “polvo”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Spanish polvos (singular),[1] from Vulgar Latin *pulvus, neuter form derived from Classical Latin pulvis m, from Proto-Indo-European *pel- (“flour, dust”). Compare English pulverise.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpolbo/ [ˈpol.β̞o]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -olbo
  • Syllabification: pol‧vo

Noun

[edit]

polvo m (plural polvos)

  1. dust (fine, dry particles of matter found in the air and covering the surface of objects)
  2. powder, dust (fine particles of a dry substance)
    • 2024 April 29, Peter Valdes-Dapena, “Rolls-Royce amplía su fábrica para construir coches más despacio”, in CNN en Español‎[2]:
      Sencillamente, cada vez hay más ricos en el mundo y tienen más dinero para gastar en cosas como coches con polvo de diamante en la pintura y equipamiento de picnic integrado en el maletero.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
  3. (vulgar, colloquial) fuck, screw (sexual intercourse)
    Synonyms: (Spain) folleteo, (Latin America) cogida
    • 1994, José Ángel Mañas, chapter XIV, in Historias del Kronen, Barcelona: Ediciones Destino, →ISBN, page 220:
      ¿Dónde están Pedro y su cerda? ( ) Han salido al jardín, seguro. ( ) Ven, Roberto, que vamos a ver un polvo en primer plano.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
  4. (plural only) see polvos

Related terms
